subject: Tenant vaulting + nodepair provisioning — intake and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Sara Taylor <sara.taylor@acmelabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmelabs.com
Date: Wed, 20 Nov 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: New: Tenant vaulting + nodepair provisioning for Acme private cluster

Neha — thanks for taking this. We're preparing to host Redwood Private in our primary facility (PHX) and have two core asks: 1) tenant-level vaulting so each tenant's secrets and keys are isolated and auditable, and 2) a "nodepair" provisioning pattern — we want pairs of identical node roles across two racks (for host-level redundancy) with clear PV failover semantics.

High level constraints:
- No public egress except via our NAT clusters (we will supply IP ranges).
- KMS must be via our on-prem HSM (Thales) and integrated with Redwood's control plane for key wrapping.
- Snapshot replication to our on-site archive (weekly) and offsite S3 (monthly).
- Expected initial fleet: 12 nodepairs (24 nodes), mixed GPU + CPU profiles.

I've attached our initial provisioning spreadsheet and a simple network sketch. Can you confirm what we need for the preflight and what acceptance tests look like from Redwood's side? Also please call out anything that would require changes to our rack-level switch configs (VLANs, LACP, MTU).

Attachments: acme-provisioning-reqs.xlsx

— Sara Taylor
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Labs
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Taylor <sara.taylor@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Nov 2029 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New: Tenant vaulting + nodepair provisioning for Acme private cluster

Sara — thanks, this is clear and very helpful. Quick readout from our side and the preflight items we'll need to lock the runbook. I've attached a small inventory template we've used before (provisioning-inventory.csv) — please populate NIC models, switch vendor & firmware, and exact NAT IPs.

Redwood preflight / acceptance checklist (summary):
- Network: point-to-point routing or S2S VPN to Redwood control plane IPs; BGP peering optional but recommended for multi-rack failover. MTU >= 9000 for NVMe traffic recommended.
- Security/KMS: HSM integration via customer-owned KMS connector (we support Thales HSM over KMIP); we'll run a key-wrapping test (encrypt/decrypt cycle) during cutover.
- Nodepair pattern: We define a nodepair as 2 nodes with identical labels and anti-affinity rules. Our recommended PV model is local-csi-replicated (copies written synchronously to the paired node's NVMe) — this provides host-level continuity without remote NFS.
- Storage: ephemeral NVMe for KV caches (configured with 30s flush and eviction TTLs), persistent volumes for model artifacts on 1 TB mirrored NVMe per nodepair, and snapshot policy (weekly local snapshots + replicated archive).
- Routing/egress: allowlist of Redwood control-plane IPs + NAT egress ranges. We'll need a transport route for metrics streaming and for agent heartbeats (TLS 443).
- Kubernetes policy: POD anti-affinity across nodepairs, node taints for reserved GPU workloads, and RBAC rules for tenant vault access.

Acceptance tests (we will run these with you during cutover):
1) KV cache performance sanity (write/read under 90th pct latency)
2) Failover drill: simulate single-node loss in a nodepair and validate PV mount and pod restart within SLA (target: app-level recovery within 90s).
3) KMS round-trip + audit log proof (we submit an encrypted blob and verify audit record in your SIEM).
4) Network egress and NAT validation (ingress blocked from internet).

Open Qs for Acme:
- Do you require synchronous replication to the archive for any tenants (we treat archive as eventual by default)?
- Can you share the switch models and whether routed interfaces already exist between the two racks?

Next steps: if you can populate the inventory and share the network diagram link we'll schedule a 60-minute preflight on Fri. I'll capture runbook tasks and attach the DocuSign link for the reserved hardware agreement once we lock scope.

Attachments: provisioning-inventory.csv

Thanks — Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Neha — inventory and a nicer network diagram are live here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmE-Designs/diagrams (see file: phx-network-v2.drawio).

Answers inline:
- We'll need synchronous snapshots for our PCI tenants, so those will be in the SLO bucket and should replicate to on-site archive immediately.
- Switches are Arista 7060CX-32; we currently run MLAG between the two top-of-rack pairs and have routed interfaces in place. MTU is set to 9000.
- NAT ranges: 198.51.100.0/24 (egress), control-plane allowlist will be provided in the next message.

Also: one operational question — for the nodepair local-csi-replicated model, what happens to PVs that are >2 TB? We have a subset of large model artifacts that exceed that size. Do you recommend externals (iSCSI) for those or a hybrid approach?

— Sara
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Taylor <sara.taylor@acmelabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Nov 2029 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: New: Tenant vaulting + nodepair provisioning for Acme private cluster

Sara / Neha — thanks for the diagram and the constraints — Arista 7060 + MTU 9000 is perfect. A few engineering notes and the proposed runbook items we will include in the DocuSign SOW:

Operational decisions (Rishi):
- Large PVs (>2 TB): recommend hybrid model. Keep model checkpoints on a separate block store (iSCSI or Ceph RBD) mounted as ReadOnly for inference pods, while training/artifact writes happen to dedicated host-attached block volumes off the nodepair. This avoids replicating huge PVs synchronously across nodepairs and still provides fast local access for hot reads.
- KMS / HSM: we'll use an HSM proxy running in a tenant-isolated control plane namespace; all requests from the Redwood agent will go through outbound TLS to your KMIP endpoint. We'll schedule an integration test for the KMIP certificate exchange.
- Nodepair provisioning flow:
  1) Provision nodepair with identical labels (nodepair-id + role).
  2) Apply local-csi-replicated StorageClass with replication to device on sibling node.
  3) Run failure-injection test (power cycle one node).
  4) Validate snapshot replication to local archive and offsite sync job kick.

Acceptance criteria we'll sign off on in SOW:
- Successful KMS roundtrip and SIEM audit event for every encryption key created during the test.
- PV mount and pod startup on sibling node within 90s in 9/10 trials.
- Snapshot created within policy window and visible in archive bucket with checksum match.

Runbook QA items (deliverables):
- Finalized inventory (your team) + NIC driver checks (our team)
- Preflight meeting (Fri 30 Nov, 10:00 PT) — we will invite NetEng and Infra owners.
- DocuSign: acme-malp-io-contract.pdf (we'll push the SOW with acceptance criteria).

I'll take ownership of the failover drills and one canary nodepair for the first week of cutover. Marissa / Laura — can one of you take primary for customer success coordination?

— Rishi Malhotra
Infrastructure Lead (On-Prem Deployments), Redwood Inference
